title: Dynamic Retail Inventory Schema Evolution
business: Retailers managing global inventory systems that require frequent schema updates to accommodate new regional product attributes without interrupting ongoing analytical reporting.
problem: Traditional data lake formats often require full table rewrites when adding or renaming columns, leading to significant downtime and high compute costs during schema evolution.
solution: Apache Iceberg utilizes metadata-based schema evolution, allowing structural changes like adding, renaming, or reordering columns without rewriting underlying data files, while maintaining consistent snapshots for concurrent readers.
steps: Identify the current table schema using the catalog metadata.
Execute an ALTER TABLE command to add or rename the required product attribute column.
Verify the schema change via the Iceberg metadata layer without triggering a data rewrite.
Perform a new write operation to populate the updated schema in new data files.
Query the table using time travel to validate both historical and current data states.
outcome: The system achieves seamless schema agility, enabling developers to evolve table structures in real-time while ensuring that long-running analytical queries remain isolated from structural changes through snapshot consistency.
limitation: Metadata-only schema evolution can lead to increased metadata file accumulation over time, which may impact catalog performance; check this by monitoring the frequency and size of metadata file commits.

By creating a copy of the entire table for every change
